content.text:
I've submitted index 10 (Ge 0.34 / Mn 0.66) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 1.5×10⁻⁷ A. I don't know how close that is to the library's best: only 3 of the 28 compositions were measured.

| Index | Ge fraction | Phase expected there | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **10** | 0.34 | Mn₂GeO₄ | **1.5×10⁻⁷** |
| 22 | 0.23 | Mn₂GeO₄ + Mn₃O₄ mix | 6×10⁻⁸ |
| 19 | 0.50 | MnGeO₃ | 5×10⁻⁸ |

- **Why I picked these three:** the band-gap model predicts about 2.0 eV for Mn₂GeO₄ and 2.1–2.6 eV for the two MnGeO₃ structures. That is below the 3.22 eV light, so both phases should absorb it. The stability model puts both close to stable. Index 10 and index 19 sit at those two compositions.
- **Third measurement:** the curve-fitting tool suggested index 22, on the Mn-rich side. It came in lower than index 10, so photocurrent seems to peak near the Mn₂GeO₄ composition rather than keep rising with more Mn.
- **Ge-rich end (Ge above 0.6):** I didn't measure it. Ge oxide doesn't absorb at this photon energy, and photocurrent dropped from Ge 0.34 to Ge 0.50, so I expected lower values there.

I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phases in the table are expected from composition, not confirmed.
